anita: Thanks everyone for joining the infra update. Quick follow-up thread for the region prioritization + autoscale specifics we discussed. High-level: prewarm for eu-west and us-west in Q2, APAC remains burst-first while we validate local partners. Drop questions here and we'll post the runbook link soon.

raj: When you say 'burst-only' for APAC, does that mean no reserved capacity? What happens to latency-sensitive customers if spot supply dries up?

lead-sre: Good q. 'Burst-only' = no dedicated reserved GPUs in the short term. We will rely on pre-warmed nodes in nearby regions + model fallbacks. Latency-sensitive routes get two-tier routing: prefer local region, fallback to nearest prewarm (us-west/eu-west) with a 200ms additional latency budget. For extreme tail we have automatic model-fallback to a lower-memory variant.

ellie: Can you share numbers for prewarm targets and prewarm window? Ops needs that to estimate cost.

lead-sre: Prewarm targets (initial): eu-west: 800 concurrent tokens/s equivalent, us-west: 1200 tokens/s. Prewarm window: 5 minutes by default, can be shortened to 90s for hot routes. Ramp policy: linear over prewarm_seconds. Example config: ```yaml
autoscaler:
  min_replicas: 0
  max_replicas: 40
  target_rps: 1200
  prewarm_seconds: 300
  burst_capacity_percent: 20
```

miguel: How do we calculate tokens/s -> replicas? Is there a public perf profile for the models we plan to prewarm?

lead-sre: We use model perf matrix in console -> model catalog. Short formula: replicas = ceil(target_tokens_per_sec / model_tokens_per_sec_per_gpu). We'll publish a simple converter doc in the runbook. Example: 1200 tokens/s / 150 tokens/s per GPU = 8 replicas.

ops-pm: Cost question — any cap on burst spend while we validate APAC?

anita: Yes. We'll set a soft-burst budget of $15k/month for APAC pilot, with automatic throttling if we hit 85% of the budget for the month. Ops will surface exact thresholds in the runbook.

raj: Fallback models — which exact variants? We need to know for quality gating.

lead-sre: Initial fallback chain (short): 1) same model, quantized variant (q8) 2) smaller architecture (redwood-7b-q8) 3) rerank only + cached responses. We'll tie fallbacks to route-level tolerances; product will have to opt-in per route.

ellie: Any changes to canary percentages for regional rollouts? We ran into an issue last time with 5% causing noisy metrics.

lead-sre: We'll default to 2% canary for new region rollouts with a 30m observation window and automated rollback on error rate >1% or latency p95 increase >30%. Ops can override per-release.

sre-bot: [alert] 2024-12-11 15:12 UTC — short capacity dip detected in us-west, auto-fallback engaged, user impact mitigated. Investigating root cause.

miguel: Is there a playbook for that alert?

ops-pm: We're updating the runbook to include that incident pattern. Action item: ana will add the exact triage steps + log queries by EOD.
